title: Fine-Tuning Safety Degradation Rate: How Many Benign Examples Does It Take?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: users fine-tuning on benign data may inadvertently degrade safety. Characterizing the degradation rate gives concrete safe fine-tuning guidance. Each link is explicit and the finding is immediately actionable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires multiple fine-tuning runs of a 7B+ model at varying dataset sizes, which demands significant GPU time and fine-tuning expertise (LoRA setup, hyperparameter management). Beyond beginner level even with Colab Pro.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple fine-tuning runs and evaluations needed. The degradation curve is a clear deliverable, but executing 4-5 fine-tuning experiments plus evaluation is sustained effort for 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: This question is substantially answered by existing work. 'Fine-tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety, Even When Users Do Not Intend To!' (ICLR 2024) demonstrated that as few as 10 adversarial examples can jailbreak GPT-3.5 Turbo. 'Fine-Tuning Lowers Safety and Disrupts Evaluation Consistency' (2025) and 'Why LLM Safety Guardrails Collapse After Fine-Tuning: A Similarity Analysis' (2025) characterize the degradation mechanism. 'Purifying Finetuning Data to Preserve LLM Safety Alignment' (EMNLP 2025) and 'Rethinking Safety in LLM Fine-tuning: An Optimization Perspective' (2025) offer mitigations. The degradation rate with benign data is a well-studied phenomenon.
